items.q: What does Scull say we actually have, if not cures?
items.a: **Symptomatic treatments.** Insulin for type-1 diabetes is the honest analogy: lives change, the disease stays. There is **no psychiatric penicillin**. Overstate the 1950s accidents and you repeat the 80% story.

items.q: What did Insel say $20B of NIMH science bought?
items.a: **Cool genetics and neuroscience.** The lot of the mentally ill **did not improve one bit**. Hyman and Insel had treated mental illness as **brain disease**. Eisenberg: the field went from **brainless to mindless**.

items.q: What did DSM-III buy after Rosenhan and the 1960s reliability mess?
items.a: **Reliability, not validity.** Two doctors tick the same symptom box. That is not a disease. Insel and Hyman later called DSM-5 **unscientific**. Drug companies and insurers still liked the codes.

items.q: What replaced the asylum for the seriously ill?
items.a: A **community-care shell game** with no pea. Cycle: short ward, gutter, jail. The three largest US 'inpatient' sites are **LA County, Cook County, and Rikers**. Mortality gap **15–25 years**, growing.

items.q: What was Henry Cotton's focal-sepsis program?
items.a: Pull teeth, tonsils, then **stomachs, spleens, colons** to stop toxins hitting the brain. Claimed **80%**. **45%** of abdominal cases dead in a year. A dentist kept pulling until **1960**.

Ice-pick through the orbit after a few shocks. **Lobotomobile** summers. **20–30** in an afternoon. 'I could teach any damn fool in twenty minutes, even a psychiatrist.' Moniz still got the **1949 Nobel**.

items.q: What did CATIE 2005 show about second-generation antipsychotics?
items.a: **Not more efficacious** than a cheap first-gen. **67–82%** dropped out. Less tardive dyskinesia, more **weight / diabetes / heart**. No biomarker for who is in which third.

items.q: How do SSRIs beat placebo in Scull's reading?
items.a: **Statistically, often not clinically** (1–2 points on a 60-point scale). Flatten affect and libido. Getting off can be worse than the illness. **NICE: CBT first.** The serotonin-deficit ad was marketing.
